questions.stem:
Statement: 'If you want to lose weight effectively, join our gym and follow our certified trainer's programme.'

Assumption I: Joining a gym under a certified trainer is an effective method for weight loss.
Assumption II: The person being addressed wants to lose weight.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: the statement recommends the gym programme specifically for weight loss — this only makes sense if the speaker assumes it actually works. Assumption II is implicit: the conditional 'If you want to lose weight' assumes the reader has that goal — otherwise the statement would not be directed at them. Both are necessary background beliefs for the statement to be meaningful.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The train to Delhi leaves at 6:00 AM; you must leave home by 4:30 AM at the latest.'

Assumption I: The journey from the person's home to the station takes at least 1.5 hours.
Assumption II: The train will depart on time at 6:00 AM.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: the specific advice to leave by 4:30 AM for a 6:00 AM train only makes sense if the speaker assumes the travel time is around 1.5 hours. Assumption II is implicit: the advice to arrive by 6:00 AM is only useful if the speaker assumes the train will actually leave at that time. Both are unstated but necessary premises.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Wear a helmet every time you ride a motorcycle — it can save your life.'

Assumption I: Motorcycles are more dangerous than other vehicles on the road.
Assumption II: Helmets reduce the severity of head injuries in accidents.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: B is correct. Assumption II is implicit: the statement that wearing a helmet 'can save your life' directly assumes that helmets provide life-saving protection — otherwise the advice has no basis. Assumption I is NOT implicit: the statement does not compare motorcycles to other vehicles; it simply advises helmet use while riding one. A comparative claim (motorcycles are more dangerous) is not assumed — the statement works without that belief.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Please submit your application online — it is faster and more convenient than visiting the office.'

Assumption I: The online application system is currently functional and accessible.
Assumption II: The applicant has access to the internet and a device to apply online.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: recommending the online system assumes it is working — there is no point advising its use if it were known to be down. Assumption II is implicit: the advice to apply online only makes sense if the speaker assumes the applicant can actually access the internet. Without internet access, the recommendation is meaningless. Both are unstated but necessary.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Students who score above 95% in the entrance exam will be offered admission to the engineering programme.'

Assumption I: Some students will score above 95% in the entrance exam.
Assumption II: Students who score above 95% are academically suited for the engineering programme.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: announcing admission criteria assumes the speaker believes some students will meet them — announcing an impossible standard would be purposeless. Assumption II is implicit: using a cutoff of 95% to grant admission assumes that this score is a reliable proxy for suitability — otherwise the criterion is arbitrary. Both underpinnings are implicit in the admission policy.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Do not park near the fire hydrant — emergency vehicles need clear access at all times.'

Assumption I: Fire hydrants are sometimes used by emergency services in this area.
Assumption II: Parked vehicles can block access to fire hydrants.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: B is correct. Assumption II is implicit: the instruction 'do not park near the fire hydrant' only makes sense if parking there would actually block access — this causal link is the unstated premise. Assumption I is NOT implicit: the instruction does not require that the hydrant has actually been used or will be used — it is a general safety rule applicable regardless of past or future use frequency. The instruction holds even if the hydrant is rarely used; the point is access must always be clear.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Reading fiction regularly improves empathy and emotional intelligence in both children and adults.'

Assumption I: Most people in society read fiction on a regular basis.
Assumption II: Empathy and emotional intelligence are desirable qualities worth developing.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: B is correct. Assumption II is implicit: the statement promotes the benefits of fiction for empathy, which only makes sense as advice or information if the speaker assumes those qualities are worth having. Assumption I is NOT implicit: the statement claims that reading fiction WOULD improve empathy — it does not assume that most people currently do read fiction. The claim can be true whether or not most people are already fiction readers.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'To boost exports, the government should provide tax exemptions to manufacturing companies.'

Assumption I: Tax exemptions will lead to increased production and exports by manufacturing companies.
Assumption II: The current tax structure is one of the reasons for low exports.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: recommending tax exemptions to boost exports assumes this policy will actually achieve that goal — the causal link (tax relief → more production → more exports) is the implicit premise. Assumption II is implicit: the specific recommendation of tax relief to boost exports implies the speaker believes current taxes are constraining exports. If taxes were irrelevant to exports, tax exemptions would not be the suggested remedy.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Install solar panels on your rooftop and reduce your monthly electricity bills by up to 70%.'

Assumption I: Solar panels are available for purchase and installation in the area.
Assumption II: The person addressed currently has high monthly electricity bills.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit: recommending solar panel installation assumes they can actually be obtained and installed — the advice is pointless if they're unavailable. Assumption II is NOT implicit: the statement offers a 70% reduction in bills without assuming the current bills are particularly high — even someone with modest bills might benefit from a 70% reduction. The statement addresses anyone with an electricity bill, not specifically those with high bills. The promise of savings works regardless of current bill size.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'All passengers must carry a valid ID proof at the time of boarding the train.'

Assumption I: Some passengers may not carry ID proof unless reminded.
Assumption II: Railway authorities can verify ID documents at the time of boarding.

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both Assumption I and Assumption II are implicit
Neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: issuing a reminder to 'must carry' ID implies the speaker expects some passengers would otherwise not carry it — announcements aren't made about things everyone always does. Assumption II is implicit: requiring ID at boarding assumes there is a system to check it — otherwise the rule serves no purpose. Both are practical preconditions for the rule to be meaningful and enforceable.
